newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MAY 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Yesterday's brief meeting in Paris between Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Turkish President Suleyman Demirel was overshadowed by the negative climate created by Demirel and Turkish deputy foreign minister Onur Oymen's comments and appeared to be an ill omen of the fate of the procedural dialogue between the two countries on resolving their differences. Simitis said Athens did not agree with the positions expressed recently by Demirel and Oymen and that Turkey must meet conditions previously set by Greece before there could be any dialogue.
--The Bank of Greece is not yet concerned about the recent outflows of foreign capital, despite the pressure on the drachma yesterday after 400 million dollars left the country.

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys has said he is dissatisfied with the rate of inflows from tax collection, ahead of reports that rates for May will once again be well below budget forecasts. There are also reports of dissatisfaction in the ministry with the new economic crimes squad and plans to remove 50 officials from duty, following reports of corruption.
--A recent study has shown that Greeks believe high-profile industrialists, the media and even the Church to be more powerful than the government and the Parliament.
--Plans to revise the Constitution may pave the way to the establishment of private universities, following yesterday's meeting of ruling party PASOK's Executive.

--Olympic Airways'- Greece's national carrier - restructuring plans came up against another obstacle over the weekend when cabin crews refused to work on their rostered days off, resulting in Serbian and Irish airliners being leased to carry out OA scheduled flights.
--Greeks drink the least beer per head in Europe, according to a new study.

--The recent green line conciliation and friendship concert by Greek and Turkish pop idols in Cyprus continues to make waves amongst the Greek entertainment scene, with actress Vanna Barbra calling the concert "idiocies".
--Leader of conservative opposition New Democracy Costas Karamanlis said that Greece must have private universities, during his presentation of ND's positions on education.

--Deputy Interior Minister Tassos Mantellis yesterday sent an urgent circular to public services regarding the need to address the problem of the changeover in dates at the end of the century and the havoc it could wreak on computers in the public service.

--Former conservative prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis said yesterday that 1989 - the year of the Koskotas embezzlement scandal, and of the special court trial of late PASOK founder Andreas Papandreou and others - was the year of "shame".
